claims.claim: Required item, part, joint and target names and basic cabinet envelope are present.
claims.evidence: asset/model.urdf: robot drawer_cabinet; root carcass, drawer and fixed-mounted handle; drawer_slide is prismatic along +X with limits 0 to 0.24 m. asset/asset.json annotations map drawer_opening to tray_floor. readings.json collision_boxes give carcass dimensions X/Y/Z = 0.30/0.42/0.25 m and 0.022 m legs; total depth including the projecting handle is 0.37 m. renders/front.png, side.png, top.png and iso.png show the expected single-drawer cabinet.

claims.claim: The tray satisfies the required minimum interior dimensions and close fit inside the carcass.
claims.evidence: readings.json collision_boxes and probes/02_geometry.out: interior X/Y/Z = 0.180/0.356/0.160 m. X is 0.070 m below the required 0.250 m minimum. The rear gap at closure is 0.077 m, rather than a few millimetres; lateral gaps are 0.004 m and front-panel top/bottom gaps are 0.002 m. Actual dimensions in asset/model.py agree with the compiled geometry; its comment claiming 0.252 m interior depth is stale.

claims.claim: Collision geometry represents the visible shell, open tray and handle without filling the usable interior.
claims.evidence: All four renders, asset/model.py geometry definitions, asset/model.urdf collision boxes and probes/02_geometry.out agree on four legs, shell panels, five tray panels and two handle objects. All 1944 carcass, 1080 drawer and 775 handle mesh vertices lie within their collision-box unions. Bevelled panels and the spherical knob use enclosing boxes; no collision spans the tray cavity or carcass opening. The placement simulation independently confirms the cavity is usable.

claims.claim: The drawer remains held by overlap with the carcass over its full declared travel.
claims.evidence: probes/01_motion_place.out full_open_bounds: at q=0.24 m the tray floor spans X=0.185 to 0.385 m while carcass_bottom ends at X=0.150 m. The entire drawer is 0.035 m beyond the carcass, so overlap is zero. probes/02_geometry.out confirms this separation. Overlap vanishes at q=0.205 m. The simulated joint constrains the detached-looking drawer, but this does not meet REVIEW.md's explicit overlap criterion.

claims.claim: The joint opens and closes without interpenetration and retains its released position.
claims.evidence: probes/01_motion_place.out: closed settled q=0.000130 m, released open q=0.239873 m; no cross-link overlaps deeper than 0.1 mm at q=0, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12, 0.16, 0.20 and 0.24 m. readings.json bounds show lateral and vertical separation throughout pure +X translation, and rear clearance increases with q. This verifies motion and clearance separately from the failed overlap-support requirement.

claims.claim: The handle has a reachable neck and knob suitable for an overhead grasp and +X pull.
claims.evidence: readings.json handles[0] places the grasp at (0.165,0,0.136) m. handle_neck is 12 mm across and extends 40 mm from front X=0.145 to knob X=0.185 m; handle_knob is 35 mm across. A 20 mm-wide finger centred at X=0.165 occupies X=0.155 to 0.175, clear of both the carcass top ending at X=0.150 and the knob beginning at X=0.185. The neck fits the 80 mm opening; the fixed handle_mount follows drawer_slide. renders/side.png and iso.png corroborate the exposed neck. This is a geometric grasp check, not a simulated gripper test.

claims.claim: A 4 cm object placed at drawer_opening at full opening settles inside the rim and remains there during closing.
claims.evidence: probes/01_motion_place.py uses scenario placement X=lip_local.x+q/2=0.145+0.24/2=0.265 m. probes/01_motion_place.out: after 120 frames the cube centre is (0.265,0,0.08394) m, its bottom is approximately floor top Z=0.064 m, and drawer contacts sum to 0.980 N. At full opening the interior X interval is 0.195 to 0.375 m, containing the cube footprint 0.245 to 0.285 m. After closing and 60 settling frames the cube is at (0.02478,0,0.08394) m, still inside; reopening retains it at (0.26487,0,0.08394) m.

metrics.feedback: Extend the drawer rearward while keeping the front panel and 0.24 m travel. For example, move tray_back centre X from -0.050 to -0.122 m, extend tray_floor to X=[-0.127,0.145] (length 0.272 m, centre 0.009 m), and extend both side panels to X=[-0.117,0.135] (length 0.252 m, centre 0.009 m). This provides 0.252 m clear interior depth, 5 mm closed rear clearance to carcass_back, and 37 mm overlap with the carcass at full extension. Update the visual meshes and collision boxes together, retain drawer_opening on tray_floor, and regenerate readings. Recheck the full travel and object placement after rebuilding.
